target.title: fix(ui): make session history accessible in picker and sidebar
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Related to #95601. This PR covers the current Control UI derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice for session history; picker/sidebar rename controls are intentionally outside this narrowed patch.

Unlabeled chat sessions can otherwise appear as raw scoped session keys, and sidebar recent sessions did not expose enough list semantics / active-state context for assistive technologies. The current branch is limited to readable derived session titles, sidebar list semantics, and proof that readable titles survive normal session patch refreshes.

## Summary

- Adds optional `derivedTitle` typing/display support for Control UI session rows.
- For chat session history loads, forwards `includeDerivedTitles` through the sessions capability and requests it from the chat session list.
- Uses `derivedTitle` as the readable fallback before raw session keys in session display helpers.
- Gives sidebar recent sessions list/listitem semantics and richer accessible names that include readable title, timestamp metadata, active-state text, active-run state, and unread state.
- Marks the active sidebar session link with `aria-current="page"`.
- Preserves durable `sessions.list` filters when refreshing after `sessions.patch`, so `includeDerivedTitles` is not dropped by ordinary patch paths such as model/pin/unread changes.
- Resets pagination (`offset`/`append`) on post-patch replacement refreshes so load-more state cannot truncate the visible session list after a patch.
- Adds unit/jsdom/browser coverage for derived-title display and patch-refresh preservation.

## Scope / Overlap Note

This PR is now the narrower derived-title + sidebar-accessibility slice. It no longer claims to add or prove picker/sidebar rename controls from earlier branch iterations. Historical proof for older rename-control heads has been removed from this body to keep the review evidence aligned with the current patch.

Because the rename-control portion is no longer in this PR, this body uses `Related to #95601` rather than a closing `Fixes` reference.

This PR should be reviewed as a partial Control UI accessibility step. The broader VoiceOver/session-history issue should remain open unless maintainers explicitly decide this narrowed derived-title/sidebar-accessibility scope is sufficient to close it.

## Compatibility / Migration

No migration is required.

- `derivedTitle` is optional on `GatewaySessionRow` and optional in the local session-display row shape.
- Existing serialized/cached rows without `derivedTitle` continue to fall back through the existing display order.
- The patch-refresh change only reuses the last successful durable list options and explicitly drops transient pagination (`offset`/`append`) for replacement refreshes.
- It does not alter persisted session data or the `sessions.patch` RPC payload.

## Evidence

Current head: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`  
CI run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867573968>  
Real behavior proof run: <https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28867610754>

The CI run completed successfully for this exact head. The proof below uses the current-head `dist-runtime-build` artifact from that CI run, not a local build.

Patch-quality evidence added in this head:

- `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts`
  - verifies `sessions.patch` refreshes preserve durable prior list options
  - specifically asserts `includeDerivedTitles: true` survives the post-patch `sessions.list`
  - covers load-more followed by `sessions.patch`, asserting the post-patch replacement refresh drops `offset` and `append` while keeping filters
  - confirms the patch RPC payload stays unchanged (`key`, `agentId`, patch fields only)
- `ui/src/e2e/chat-flow.e2e.test.ts`
  - browser/DOM test sets up two `sessions.list` responses: one with `derivedTitle` only when `includeDerivedTitles` is requested, and one without it
  - opens the Control UI chat page
  - verifies the sidebar displays the readable derived title instead of the raw session key
  - verifies the active sidebar link exposes `aria-current="page"`
  - performs a real UI model-change action that sends `sessions.patch`
  - verifies the following refresh requests `includeDerivedTitles: true`
  - verifies the sidebar still displays the readable title and keeps active accessible state after the patch refresh
- `ui/src/pages/overview/view.render.test.ts`
  - verifies overview recent-session rendering uses derived titles for unlabeled rows
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
  - verifies chat session list requests include derived titles
- `git diff --check`: passed before push
- Conflict scan: no unmerged files and no conflict markers before push

## Current-Head Real Gateway Browser Media Proof

Proof packet: <https://gist.github.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890>

Real Gateway report: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/fc207111a28457284634e32e86885e00dae621e7/REAL_GATEWAY_REPORT.md>  
Sanitized proof JSON: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/367e4b57e526d9dc0dee1ce12cd885424c85b31d/real-gateway-proof.public.json>  
Browser video: <https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/bb68812f015abddc6068921411ef6c2f5020b9af/pr-96267-real-gateway-browser-proof.webm>

This proof uses the current-head Control UI `dist-runtime-build` artifact from CI and a real foreground OpenClaw Gateway running against an isolated temporary state dir. It does not mock the Gateway websocket. The page records real Gateway RPC methods while using synthetic session data only.

Real setup details:

- Control UI static assets: current-head CI artifact for `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`
- Gateway: real OpenClaw Gateway, loopback-only, isolated temporary state
- Browser: Chromium served from the same origin as the real Gateway (`http://127.0.0.1:19089/`)
- Session data: synthetic transcript/session store
- Mock Gateway: `false`

Flow:

1. Seed synthetic sessions in the real Gateway session store.
2. Open PR-head Control UI chat page in Chromium.
3. Select `agent:dev:proof-target`.
4. Verify sidebar renders `Readable planning title` from `derivedTitle`, not the raw key.
5. Call the actual page runtime `context.sessions.patch(...)`, exercising `ui/src/lib/sessions/index.ts` against the real Gateway.
6. Verify the UI sends real `sessions.patch` and then refreshes with `sessions.list` + `includeDerivedTitles: true`.
7. Verify the readable title and active accessible state remain after the patch refresh.

Assertions captured in `real-gateway-proof.public.json`:

- `head`: `8db3480d78bd5c07b733b018a27f30dcaaf06eb3`
- `usedMockGateway`: `false`
- `uiPatchAttempt.succeeded`: `true`
- `uiPatchAttempt.note`: `runtime.context.sessions.patch sent sessions.patch and refreshed with includeDerivedTitles`
- visible sidebar label: `Readable planning title`
- row/link accessible label: `Readable planning title · just now · Active`
- active link state: `aria-current="page"`
- real patch request: `sessions.patch` for `agent:dev:proof-target`, model `openai/gpt-5.5`
- post-patch refreshes with `includeDerivedTitles: true`: `3`

Before patch / active sidebar state on real Gateway:

![Readable derived title active sidebar proof on real Gateway](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/cf4e594403087470ef090810c502681b4f880e76/01-real-gateway-derived-title-active-sidebar.png)

After real UI `sessions.patch` / derived title preserved:

![Derived title preserved after session patch proof on real Gateway](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/snowzlmbot/20e1e76e1359aa94c69c21f714234890/raw/6ea6c193b79ccdbda504212852bb65d623ae8e3c/02-real-gateway-after-session-patch-title-preserved.png)

## Privacy

The media proof uses synthetic session keys, synthetic titles, and a local mock Gateway. No private user data, tokens, hostnames, or real sessions are included.

## Not Tested

- Live macOS VoiceOver speech transcript was not re-captured for this narrower current-head patch. The browser/DOM proof verifies the accessible names and active state that screen readers consume.
